units.account: Col. Aubry held his line on the south bank as ordered, opened files to let the returning squadron pass to his rear, and watched the enemy column come down to the far end of the bridge, out of musket range.
Col. Delacroix kept his battalion in line covering the bridge exit, not stirring a man, and watched enemy infantry and horse arrive on the far bank.

Maj. Verneuil held the picket and fired carbines at the enemy column as it came down the road, itching to charge. When the infantry pressed on and hussars swung round his left to cut him off, he did as written: fell back over the bridge at the trot, losing a few men to musketry and a brush with the hussars, and re-formed behind the 1st Battalion.
units.departure: The engine left the squadron standing in front of a battalion column for 13 minutes of fire until morale fell to 29. Its order says to fall back over the bridge if pressed by infantry, so it withdrew early with light losses (11 men, not 38) to behind the 1st Battalion, about 600 m from the projected spot.

units.account: Col. Brandt marched the moment the order came, column down the high road. The enemy horse picket at the bridge fired carbines and then gave way before his leading companies' volleys, retiring over the bridge. He halted at the north end of the bridge, master of this bank, with enemy lines in sight beyond.
units.departure: Ammunition: the column fired only a few volleys at a picket that gave way, not 13 minutes of fire, so ammo stays at 92, not 30.

units.account: Col. Hartmann, with no new orders, held his column on the road and rested his men.

Maj. von Reiter rode on the column's right to get between the enemy horse and the bridge. The enemy did not stand: his leading troop caught their rear in a brief scuffle before they crossed. He drew rein at the river bank rather than follow onto a bridge covered by enemy infantry.

summary: Turn 2 (20-40). Red's Vanguard Battalion marched down the high road on receiving its order at minute 4, with the hussars riding on its right. The Blue cavalry picket at the north end of the bridge fired carbines at the column, then, pressed by infantry and with hussars working round its flank, followed its standing order and fell back over the bridge, losing 11 men in the exchange and a brief brush with the hussars. It re-formed behind the 1st Battalion. By minute 40 the Vanguard holds the north end of the bridge in column, with the hussars beside it on the bank. Red's Line Battalion stayed in reserve on the road. Blue's two battalions hold their line on the south bank, about 320 m from the bridge's north end, so no fire was exchanged across the river. The bridge itself is uncontested.
